data.headline: Raise price 2% starting week 3; hold stock and supplier
data.why: The model shows this plan adds the most profit versus keeping prices flat or cutting them. It beats the rival's lower price because nearly half your customers already prefer you and the increase is small enough to keep most of them.
data.watch_out: If rice costs jump more than expected, your margin shrinks fast because rice is 20% of cost. Watch supplier prices weekly; a bad case is cost rising 5%+ while you cannot pass it on.
data.recheck_when: Recheck at week 3 when the price change hits, or sooner if Mekong Delta rice quotes move sharply.
data.cost_line: Rice +20% × 20% of your cost is rice = your cost +4% (+$0.04 a plate)

fixed: Fixed costs such as rent and salaries (profit here is gross profit)
Payment terms (we assume you pay suppliers when you order, and customers pay when they buy)
How other rivals react (we model one main rival)

flags.text: Worse than headline: Rice +30% plus demand down (cost up and demand down together).
Also we want to address weak spots: for raise price, worst is s2 (Rice +30% & demand -20%) with -10.3k bad case, drag from customers lost.
…ise price 5% now" is terrible - loses customers heavily, especially in s2 (Rice +30% & demand -20%) with -10.3k bad case.
Marketing only: "Marketing +30%" - try to gain share without price increase.

what_happened.text: India banned exports of non-basmati white rice, effective at once.
Vietnam's 5% broken rice export price rose to its highest since 2011.
Vietnamese 5% broken rice reached $638 a tonne, $105 above its level the day before India's ban.
The World Bank's monthly price was $616 a tonne, up from $455 in April.

caveats: Rice is about a fifth of a plate's cost in the owner's own words. Prices in VND are converted at 25,000 VND = $1, the app's fixed rate.
The series is Vietnam's rice EXPORT price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/mt). Rice bought at home moved less than the export price, so the swing scored here is larger than the restaurant's.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.
